//: FILE: package.json  -  the project's 'ID card and instruction sheet'
This is a JSON file. JSON does NOT allow normal comments (adding them
would stop npm from reading the file). So the explanations are stored
in extra entries whose names start with // (like this one). npm
officially ignores entries named this way, so they change nothing.
JSON basics: everything is written as  "name": value  pairs inside
curly brackets { }. Text is in double quotes. Lists use [ ].
WHAT THIS FILE DOES, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
npm (Node Package Manager, installed together with Node.js) reads this
file to learn: the project's name, which ready-made libraries it needs
to download, and what the short commands like 'npm run dev' mean.
Analogy: the label and recipe card on a meal kit - what's in the box,
THE TWO COMMANDS THAT RUN THE PROJECT
npm install  -> reads 'dependencies' below and downloads Express and
sql.js into a folder called node_modules.
npm run dev  -> looks up 'dev' under 'scripts' below and runs it.
// name: The project's name. Lower-case, no spaces (npm's rule).
name: recruiter-bot
// version: The project's version number: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. 1.0.0 = first complete version.
// description: A one-sentence summary of what the project does.
description: Recruiter Bot - ranks candidates for jobs (and jobs for candidates) using hand-written SQL on SQLite.
// main: The project's main/entry file: the one that starts everything (see src/server.js).
// scripts: SHORTCUT COMMANDS. Each entry is  "shortcut": "the real command it runs".
You type  npm run <shortcut>  (or just  npm start / npm test  for those two).
dev       -> npm run dev       Starts the server and AUTO-RESTARTS it whenever
watching for changes). Use this while working.
start     -> npm start         Starts the server once, without auto-restart.
seed      -> npm run seed      Wipes the database and reloads the 15 candidates
detective -> npm run detective Runs the Part 2 SQL Detective answers and prints
test      -> npm test          Runs the 13 automatic checks in tests/api.test.js
// engines: WHICH VERSION OF NODE.JS IS NEEDED: 18.18 or newer ('>=' means 'at least').
Older versions lack features this project uses ('node --watch', the
built-in 'fetch' used by the tests). Check yours by typing: node --version
// dependencies: READY-MADE LIBRARIES THE PROJECT NEEDS. 'npm install' downloads these.
express  - makes it easy to build a web server: we just say 'when someone
sql.js   - the SQLite database engine, packaged so it installs on any
computer without extra build tools (see src/db.js).
THE VERSION NUMBERS: '^5.1.0' means 'version 5.1.0 or any later 5.x.x
release' (the ^ allows safe updates but never a new major version 6,
which might work differently). The exact versions actually installed are
WHY ONLY TWO: fewer libraries = less to install, less to go wrong, and
less code to explain. Everything else uses tools built into Node.js.
